headline: Explicit references for judging biological model outputs in genome folding and cryo-EM
label: Evaluating Biological Model Representations
summary: Three October to November 2026 preprints test model outputs against explicit biological or measurement references rather than accepting them as opaque.
synthesis: The common thread is assessment of model outputs against explicit biological or measurement references rather than acceptance as opaque. HiFold-Mamba, a Stage 1 Registered Report, predicts 3D genome contact maps from DNA using a reverse-complement-equivariant state-space model and tests whether an insulation-based map-level constraint improves sequence-based prediction. The cryo-EM preprint introduces ramped phase randomization, a low-pass filter variant used for map comparison and neural network data augmentation, with an open-source Python implementation. The EEG study evolves spiking networks with calcium-dynamic neurons and synaptic delays for seizure detection on CHB-MIT and Siena datasets; it is less directly aligned with this evaluative thread. All three are preprints, so the evidence remains preliminary.
